title: The Singularity Is Nearer
subtitle: When We Merge with AI
pitch: Nearly twenty years later, Kurzweil checks his forecasts against large language models and doubles down: 2029 for human level AI, 2045 for the singularity.

chapters.g: Why he is writing again: AI has moved faster than most people expected, and close to his own forecasts.

chapters.t: Where Are We in the Six Stages?
chapters.g: A quick recap of the six epochs, and where we stand now.
The long road from early AI to deep learning and large language models, and why he still expects human level AI by 2029.
Consciousness, identity and what it would mean to back up or extend a mind.
Data on falling poverty, rising lifespans and cheaper energy, used to argue things are better than the news suggests.

chapters.t: The Future of Jobs: Good or Bad?
chapters.g: Automation, which jobs change, and why he expects new kinds of work and abundance.

chapters.t: The Next Thirty Years in Health and Well-Being
chapters.g: AI driven medicine, nanobots and his idea of longevity escape velocity.
Risks from biotech, nanotech and AI, including misalignment, and how he thinks they can be managed.
An imagined debate with a pessimist, testing his own optimism.

ideas: Large language models are evidence for his timeline.
Material life keeps getting better on most measures.

args.a: Exponential progress will bring abundance and longer lives.
args.c: Others argue benefits will be unevenly shared and that existential risks get too little weight.

questions: Has the arrival of ChatGPT and agents made Kurzweil look more right?
Is his peril chapter enough of an answer to safety researchers?

quiz.w: He keeps 2029 for AI passing a strong Turing test.

quiz.q: Who does Kurzweil debate in the last chapter?
quiz.w: Cassandra stands in for the pessimists.
